chapter: Blue Devils, Moten and the Reno Club
title: Willard Alexander, Hammond versus Glaser, and Basie's debt to Hammond
summary: Basie confirms part of the Willard Alexander story, says he liked John Hammond from the first night, and credits Hammond with being responsible for the band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Right, yeah. "When Benny came to the Reno Club in the spring of 1936, the year of the band, none of us was aware that he was digging us."
That's what I'm talking about.

This is where you say it's true. "Benny went back to Chicago and phoned his own booker, Willard Alexander, of Music Corporation of America in New York. In the meantime, John mentioned us to Willard and Willard made a trip to Kansas City himself and signed the band with MCA." Is that the way it happened?
Well, yeah, part of it. That's part of it.
What's the other part?
None of your business. (Unintelligible.)
Oh. Somebody told me that when he had a chance of going with John Hammond or Joe Glazer, he went with Joe Glazer because he felt that --
Who was it?
I'm not going to tell you.
Huh?
I'm not going to tell you.
I know who.
You do?
Sure.

He went with Joe because John seemed like, yeah, he was kind of like a magazine writer and didn't seem to really know the business. You know, he felt Joe Glazer really knew what was happening, could his career, I guess. Did you have any of those feelings about John or --

No, sir. Well, I'll tell you the truth, I mean, John used to write about the band all the time when he was writing on this magazine (inaudible) and he used to always say, 'I wonder why Basie doesn't write to answer this letter,' write (unintelligible) Of course, I didn't know anything about John when I met him then; he told me (inaudible) who he was. We just hung out all night, (inaudible). I liked John. From then on, it was a good friendship and then
John just sort of took hold of things (inaudible), you know. I mean, (inaudible) I don't mind telling anybody (inaudible) John's responsible for this band. (Inaudible).
Does John think he is?
Huh?
Does John think he is?
No, he doesn't. (Inaudible) no way.

I mean, he's done so much for so many people. I mean, and he's uncovered so many people that were covered up that have been great in their day and he's discovered so many, just numbers of artists, that are very big (inaudible) --
Yeah.
And he never mentions those things and I -- really, I don't think we've done quite enough for this guy. He's never asked anybody for a nickel.
Well, he didn't have to, now, did he? He had all that money.
That don't make any difference.
Yeah.
Many a booking agent is a millionaire, but they still want that money.
Right. Once you have money, you want more money.
That's right. You find very few -- you can count them all on your one finger who's going to (inaudible)
their pocket and do everything for you and don't want it back.
Yeah, it just occurs to me that the difference might be that John was born with that, which is different than having to go out and make it --
Makes a bit of difference -- we got to be born or not born with it --
(End of Side A.)
